object_description: two nearly identical volumes pushed together at a corner
design_condition: The two volumes are loosely set along the slope, spanning outdoor areas toward the existing school while preserving open green space and connecting the buildings with planted bands.

positive.statement: The outdoor areas span an arch toward the existing school building.
The delicate structure and analogous architectural language treat both new buildings identically and equally.
The facade design and loose setting are appropriate to the village context.
The planted front and break areas form a continuous connecting band between the buildings.
The large sports and playing fields correspond to the loose setting of the two buildings.
The chosen wooden construction can be assumed to be sustainable.
The internal organization of the school building seems clear.

negative.statement: The double hall receives light only through a high opening on the north side, causing an uneven distribution of daylight.
The second staircase required for fire safety remains undecided and obscures the floor-plan organization.
Delivery crosses the access area and creates conflicts during events.
Maintenance costs are comparatively high despite the expected low construction costs.
The wide central zone and sometimes large classroom depths make the building dimensions questionable for school use.
The chosen building dimensions create unsatisfactory daylight situations.
